description:
FILED s473v (2026-09-17) from the round-33 merge bar, where it cost an hour to
prove that 34 of a companion run's "36 NEW ROW / 38 FIXED ROW" were not the
round's.

THE SYMPTOM.  `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 re/subst.t` (and any file whose
TAP descriptions contain its own path) always reports:

    ROW DIFF vs baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv: ... NEW ROW ... FIXED ROW
      NEW ROW by file:   re/subst.t 14, re/pat_rt_report.t 4
      FIXED ROW by file: re/subst.t 14, re/pat_rt_report.t 4
      + re/subst.t   [at t/re/subst.t line 119]
      - re/subst.t   [at /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/build/perl-5.40.3/perl-5.40.3/t/re/subst.t line 119]

-- the SAME row, twice, in two spellings.  Because a NEW failing row makes the
run "NOT clean", a reviewer must classify all of them, every time.

THE MECHANISM (located, not guessed).  tools/lib/PclTapAlign.pm line 157:

    $desc =~ s{\Q$tdir\E/}{t/}g if defined $tdir && length $tdir;

normalises the run's descriptions.  The row set WRITTEN to .suitelog/*.fails.tsv
keeps the absolute form (verified: a direct row-by-row diff of
.suitelog/re_subst.t.fails.tsv against the baseline block finds exactly ONE
difference, the synthetic test#0 `*summary*` row -- not fourteen), so the
baseline and the log agree and only the COMPARED set is rewritten.  The
normalisation is applied on one side of the comparison only.

MEASURED BOTH WAYS, s473v: a `git archive main` extraction (5eb87b01, gen
v2-1460, the same harness) run over the same four files reports the SAME churn
-- re/subst.t 14/14, re/pat_rt_report.t 4/4, re/pat.t 16 new / 14 fixed.  So it
is not any branch's, it is the tool's, and it has presumably been there since
the row baseline was first blessed.

FIX SHAPE (either is fine, they are the same decision):
 (a) normalise on BOTH sides -- apply the same rewrite when READING
     perl-suite-fails.tsv, and re-bless the affected rows once, with the note;
 (b) or do not normalise the compared set at all, and keep the rewrite for
     DISPLAY only.
(a) is better: the absolute path embeds this machine's perlbrew root, so a
baseline carrying it is not portable between checkouts anyway (the same class
as the #217/#349 "generated artifacts embed build paths" note).

Guard: a tools/t row that runs one file twice and asserts ZERO row diff, plus
one that asserts a baseline row containing the t-dir path joins.

NOT IN SCOPE HERE: re/pat.t's OTHER churn is genuinely run-to-run -- its
descriptions contain randomly generated node names (`20000 nodes, const-len
'ax13876y25677y21378y21378kbc'`), which Fable already recorded in the s486c
merge review as differing from run to run on main too.  Same family as #1834
(the snapshot block that is never quiet) and #1835 (the bless flags rewrite the
whole file); those three together are why a companion review costs an hour.
subject: COMPANION ROW DIFF REPORTS THE SAME ROW AS *BOTH* NEW AND FIXED, FOREVER: PclTapAlign.pm:157 rewrites the t-dir prefix out of a TAP description (`$desc =~ s{\Q$tdir\E/}{t/}g`) for the set it COMPARES, while baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv holds the un-rewritten absolute form -- so every row whose description contains the test file's own path (test.pl's `_where`, i.e. `[at <file> line N]`) shows up once as `+` and once as `-` on every run; measured s473v as 14 rows in re/subst.t + 4 in re/pat_rt_report.t + part of re/pat.t's 16, IDENTICAL on a current-main extraction
